newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond negatives bring rally to an end.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond negatives bring rally to an end.

text.p: FUTURES CASH YIELD
*Bonds have see-saw day, ending in negative territory.
*RBA remains silent at rate change announcement time.
*Moody's says Australian credit rating outlook improving
*Economic data's apparent strength seen misleading

Australian bonds ended in negative territory for the first time in a week after there was no rate cut announcement forthcoming from the RBA in the morning and data suggested the economy was starting to gather steam.

Bonds had been rallying in the first hour trade ahead of the 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) announcement time of any policy change, but began to fall just prior to that time, and fell further when no announcement was made.
One positive for the bond market on the day was the announcment by Moody's Investors Services that Australia's credit rating outlook was improving.
However, after May data showed retail trade rose 2.9 percent and building approvals were up 2.2 percent, traders said sentiment favouring another rate cut had begun to wane.
"People are still trying to come to terms with exactly what the implications are for monetary policy," said Chris Bell, Director of Treasury at Dresdner Australia.
"The feeling is that we're not going to get one (a rate cut) this time around...and the jury is still out whether we'll get one in August," he said.
Treasurer Peter Costello did bonds no favours when he said the credit outlook and the data added up to a "good news day."
"A gathering convergence of economic indicators which show a very positive outlook in relation to the Australian economy," Costello told reporters after the data was released.

But while rate cut hopes were lowered, the odds were still seen at around 50 percent chance of a cut. Bonds are expected to be bid ahead of 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) on Thursday, especially if there is no hike in U.S. rates when the FOMC meeting concludes later today.
Costello did give the interest rate bulls some hope when he said the key for local rates was the RBA's inflation target, although attention was paid to offshore developments.
Second quarter inflation data later this month is expected to show annual underlying inflation underneath the RBA's two to three percent target range.
Some see the RBA waiting for this data, or possibly until after the August board meeting, before cutting rates again.
As well, some had doubts on the apparent strength in the economic data. While retail trade rose strongly, it followed two weak months, and the trend remained soft.
The building approvals data was also boosted by the inclusion of the Olympic Village in Sydney, without which approvals would have been down over 12.5 percent.

"There is still no hard evidence of the beginnings of an acceleration in economic growth needed to start to cut into the unacceptably high unemployment rates," was UBS Australia chief economist Stephen Robert's summation of the data.
AUD VS 3-YR 10-YR * AUD 3-YR/10-YR SPREAD

Spreads widen, reversing much of Tuesday's narrowing, on the disappointment at the lack of a rate cut announcement today and the perception that there may not be another coming at all. With the short end more vulnerable to pullback, the curve flattened.
